title: Installing a Water Filter with a Separate Faucet: Under-Sink Plumbing and Fittings

locations.name: kitchen sink / under-sink area
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly references mounting at the kitchen sink and drilling through the sink; mentions 'under the kitchen sink'.

summary: This Old House demonstrates installing a dedicated filtered-water faucet and an under-sink carbon-block filter. The host introduces the faucet and filter assembly, explains how the carbon block works by showing a cut block, and then guides the viewer through drilling a 3/4-inch hole in a stainless-steel kitchen sink using a slug cutter. The faucet is mounted with a backing plate and tightened with a basin wrench in a tight space. The cold-water supply is disconnected and re-routed to feed the filter, with fittings and a tee to supply the filter. The upper housing is mounted, the cartridge is installed with a quarter-turn, and the supply tubes are connected with quick-connect fittings. The video concludes with re-pressurizing the cold water and noting the cartridge life (approximately six months at around four gallons per day).

sections.title: Overview of components and filter concept
sections.description: Introduction to the new filtered-water faucet, the under-sink carbon-block filter, and how water flows through the filter to produce filtered water at the faucet.

sections.title: Faucet installation and securing it with a basin wrench
sections.description: Marking the faucet location, drilling a 3/4-inch hole with a slug cutter to avoid deforming the sink, threading the faucet through the hole, and securing the nut with a basin wrench in a tight space.

sections.title: Connecting filter to cold-water supply and mounting
sections.description: Disconnecting the cold-water side, attaching the filter fittings to the faucet, connecting the cold supply to the filter, and mounting the filter housing under the sink.

sections.title: Filter cartridge installation and system check
sections.description: Installing the filter cartridge with a quarter-turn, connecting the supply tubes, re-pressurizing the cold line, and noting an approximate cartridge life (about six months at four gallons per day).
